items.headline: Alberta non-residential building cost indexes rose in 2026 Q2
items.model_implication: Update the Alberta construction-cost baseline after validating component-level movements. Do not attribute the change to AI investment; it is a pre-scenario market observation.
items.observed_change: The non-residential building composite rose from 110.1 to 111.9 in Calgary and from 111.5 to 113.1 in Edmonton between 2026 Q1 and Q2 (2023=100). These are approximately 1.6% and 1.4% quarter-over-quarter increases, respectively; the series is not seasonally adjusted and can be revised.

items.headline: AESO's 2026 outlook design treats data-centre growth as a major uncertainty
items.model_implication: Keep multiple load-realization pathways and connection-stage probabilities in the Alberta power module rather than using a single data-centre load forecast.
items.observed_change: AESO's 2026 Long-Term Outlook engagement material explicitly identifies increased data-centre development interest as a source of uncertainty for load growth and generation needs through 2050. The final outlook has not yet been published on this page.

digest.promotion_rule: Digest evidence does not change model values until reviewed and included in a versioned release.

labour_pressure.interpretation: A screening diagnostic for recruitment pressure. It is not the Statistics Canada job vacancy rate, not a current workforce denominator and not a measure of spare capacity.
limitations: The numerator and denominator come from different surveys and reference periods.
The 2021 Census reference week occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic's third wave.
Census counts use the 25% long-form sample and random rounding.
A trade-node ranking is published only when every component NOC has a published vacancy and a positive workforce denominator.
The diagnostic does not calibrate graph-edge effect sizes or estimate project delay.

manifest.publication_note: Uncalibrated research prototype. Observations, inferences and scenarios remain explicitly separated; diagnostic scores are not findings or forecasts.

power_overlay.description: A transparent MW-based scenario overlay for possible AI data-centre load commissioned between 2027 and 2036. It is independent of the $50B capex scenario.
limitations: The power overlay is independent of the CAD capex propagation model.
Energy PUE is used only for annual energy; peak demand uses a separate peak-to-IT factor.
The planning transfer proxy is a transparent arithmetic scenario, not a grid study.
Actual requirements depend on siting, behind-the-meter supply, interconnection studies, reliability criteria and project realization.
power_overlay.name: Independent Alberta AI load and transmission overlay
power_overlay.structural_test_banner: INDEPENDENT UNCALIBRATED POWER OVERLAY — not an AESO needs assessment, generation forecast, connection approval, or transmission plan.

scenario.case_note: Low, central and high are co-moving structural weight-and-retention cases. They are not confidence bounds or a probability distribution.
scenario.description: A counterfactual structural test of how a ten-year AI infrastructure capital program could propagate through selected Alberta construction resources and public-delivery pressures. It is not a forecast or an aggregation of announced projects.

diagnostic_scale.interpretation: Monotone bounded display score only; not a probability, percentage, effect size or delay estimate.

limitations: Pressure scores are dimensionless diagnostic indices; 0.24 does not mean a 24% delay.
The graph excludes 54% of capex assigned to computing, networking, professional and other costs.
All graph weights, retention factors, absorption values, local capture and normalization denominators are declared assumptions pending calibration.
Uniform local capture is a simplifying assumption tested at 0.40, 0.72 and 0.90.
Power-system quantities are excluded from this CAD propagation model and published in an independent MW-based overlay.
